If he brings it fully, he passes to the sixth, where he is questioned about the 'umrah. If he answers it fully, he passes to the seventh, where he is questioned about wrongful deeds (mazalim). ﴿They shall not taste therein any coolness, nor any drink,﴾ It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that "coolness" (al-bard) means sleep. Al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Ubaydah said the same, and the Arabs say: "The coolness prevented (mana'a) the sleep," meaning that the coolness drove away sleep. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: "They shall not taste therein any coolness" means refreshment and rest. Ad-Dahhak said: "a place of recreation."

﴿حَدَائِقَ وَأَعْنَابًا﴾ [Gardens and grapevines], meaning the trees and fruits of Paradise.

﴿وَكَوَاعِبَ﴾ [And full-breasted maidens], young women whose breasts have become firm, singular *kā'ib* (kawā'ib), ﴿أَتْرَابًا﴾ [of equal age].

﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا﴾ [And a cup overflowing]. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: filled to the brim. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: consecutive (one after another). 'Ikrimah said: pure.

﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا﴾ [They will not hear therein any idle talk], meaning vain speech, ﴿وَلَا كِذَّابًا﴾ [nor lying], meaning falsehood; none of them will lie to another. al-Kisa'i read *kiddhaban* with a light (unstressed) *dh*, as the verbal noun of *kadhib* (kādhib), like *al-mukadhabah* (mutual lying). It is said that it means lying itself. It is also said that it has the meaning of *takdhib* (denial), like the emphatic form.

﴿جَزَاءً مِنْ رَبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا﴾ [A recompense from your Lord, a gift sufficient in reckoning], meaning He rewarded them with a reward and gave them a gift, *hisaban*, that is: sufficient and abundant, as one says, "I gave so-and-so *ahsabtu*," meaning I gave him what suffices him, until he says, "Enough for me (*hasbi*)." Ibn Qutaybah said: "*'ataan hisaban*" means abundant. It is also said: it is a recompense according to their deeds.

Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Ya'qub read *ar-Rahmani* in the genitive, following His saying "Lord of the heavens." The rest read in the nominative: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *Rabbi* in the genitive because it is near "from your Lord," and they read *ar-Rahmanu* in the nominative as a new sentence because it is further away from it. His saying ﴿لَا يَمْلِكُونَ﴾ [They do not possess] is in the place of nominative, as its predicate.

The meaning of ﴿لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًا﴾ [They will not possess from Him any speech]: Muqatil said: creation cannot speak to the Lord except by His permission. al-Kalbi said: they do not possess intercession except by His permission.

﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾: that is, on that Day. Scholars differed about this Spirit. Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said: it is Jibril (Gabriel).

'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Spirit is an angel among the angels. Allah has created no creation greater than him. On the Day of Resurrection he will stand alone in one rank, and all the angels will stand in one rank, so his size will be like theirs."[[See al-Tabari: 30/22.]]

It is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The Spirit is an angel greater than the heavens, the mountains and the angels. He is in the fourth heaven and glorifies Allah twelve [thousand][[Omitted from manuscript B.]] times every day. From each glorification an angel is created, who comes on the Day of Resurrection in a rank of his own."[[Reported by al-Tabari: 30/22. Ibn Kathir found it strange and said: "This is a very strange opinion." See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/400.]]

Mujahid, Qatadah and Abu Salih said: the "Spirit" is a creation made in the form of the children of Adam, but they are not humans. They stand in a rank, and the angels stand in a rank. These are an army and those are an army.

Mujahid reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "They are a creation in the form of the children of Adam. No angel descends from the heaven without one of them being with him."[[See al-Tabari: 30/23.]]

Al-Hasan said: they are the children of Adam.[[Reported by al-Tabari: 30/23.]] Qatadah narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas and said: "This is among the things Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal."[[The preferred view is to combine these opinions, as Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) explained: 30/23, where he said: "The correct statement is that Allah, may He be remembered, informed that His creatures do not possess speech on the Day when the Spirit stands. The Spirit is one of His creatures. It is possible that some of these things mentioned are it, and Allah knows best which of them it is. No report establishes that any one of them alone is meant, so that one must accept it, and there is no proof indicating it. Ignorance of it does no harm." See also Ibn Kathir: 4/466–467, where he preferred that they are the children of Adam.]]

﴿And the angels in ranks﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: "They are two rows (simat) of the Lord of the Worlds: on that Day one row of the Spirit stands and one row of the angels stands."

﴿None will speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and he will say what is right﴾: that is, what is true (ṣawāban, "right"). It was also said that he says: "There is no god but Allah."[[Al-Tabari reported it from 'Ikrimah. Then he said: "The correct statement is that Allah, may He be remembered, informed about His creatures that they will not speak on the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, except those among them whom the Most Merciful has permitted to speak, and who says what is right. It is obligatory to say as He informed, since He did not tell us in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger, that He meant by it one kind of what is right. The apparent meaning includes all of it."]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 78, verses 39–40:

﴿That is the true day﴾, the one that is certain to occur, meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So whoever wills may take a return (ma'ab) to his Lord﴾: a place of return and a way, through His obedience. That is: whoever wills, let him return to God through obedience to Him.

﴿Indeed We have warned you of a near punishment﴾: meaning the punishment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is near.

﴿The Day when a man will look upon what his hands have sent forward﴾: that is, every person will see on that Day the deeds he sent forward, recorded in his record of deeds. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr said: [[In the two manuscripts it reads "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar", but in al-Tabari (30/26) it is "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr", and likewise in Ibn Kathir (4/467). Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/402) attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Shahin in the book "al-ʿAjaib wa'l-Gharaʾib".]] When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched out like a hide, and the beasts, the animals and the wild creatures will be gathered. Then retaliation will be made between the animals, so that the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep that gored it. When the retaliation is finished, it will be said to them: "Be dust!" At that moment the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!" The same is related from Mujahid.

Muqatil said: God will gather the wild beasts, the creeping creatures and the birds, and He will judge between them until the hornless is avenged against the horned. Then He will say to them: "I created you and subjected you to the children of Adam, and you were obedient to them during your lives. Return to what you were; be dust!" Then, when the disbeliever looks at something, it turns to dust. He will wish and say: "Would that I were in the world in the form of a pig, and today I were dust!"

And from Abu al-Zinad ʿAbd Allah ibn Dhakwan [[In manuscript "A" it reads Abu al-Zinad ʿan ʿAbd Allah ibn Dhakwan; the correct form is that it is a single name.]] he said: When God has judged between people and commanded the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, it will be said to the rest of the nations and to the believing jinn: "Return to dust!" and they will return to dust. At that point the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!" Laith ibn [Abi] [[Omitted in manuscript "B"; the correct reading is what we have established, as in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib.]] Sulaym also said this: the believing jinn will return to dust. [[See al-Tabari 30/26.]]

It is also said that the disbeliever here is Iblis [[al-Tha'labi related from some of his teachers that he saw this in some tafsir; see Zad al-Masir 8/13. The correct view is that it is general to every disbeliever, since it does not specify a particular disbeliever, so Iblis and others are included...]], because he found fault with Adam, saying he was created from clay, and boasted that he himself was created from fire. So when on the Day of Resurrection he sees what Adam and his believing descendants have of reward and mercy, and what he himself is in of severity and punishment, he will say: "Would that I were dust!" Abu Hurayrah said: "It will be said to him: 'Dust! There is no honour for you. Who made you like me?'"
